title: B1-08 · Word phrases and nominal sentence: order and agreement

blocks.text: B1-08 · Word phrases and nominal sentence: order and agreement
Lesson overview

With the module B1.2 from the word to the sentence. The first question is simple only in appearance: in what order are subject and verb put, and how do they agree? In Arabic the answer changes according to order: ⁧وَصَلَ الوُزَرَاءُ⁩ The ministers have arrived, and the verb to the singular, ⁧الوُزَرَاءُ وَصَلُوا⁩ has the verb in plural. Newspapers write headlines under the first name ( ⁧الحُكُومَةُ تَرْفَعُ الأُجُورَ⁩ ) and the text with the verb before ( ⁧رَفَعَتِ الحُكُومَةُ الأُجُورَ⁩ ). And the plurals of things want the singular feminine: ⁧السَّيَّارَاتُ وَصَلَتْ⁩ . In this unit you put in order all these rules, which you met to pieces in A1 and A2. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 111–112), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Grammar G48, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. distinguish the verbal phrase ( ⁧الجُمْلَةُ الفِعْلِيَّةُ⁩ ) from the nominal sentence ( ⁧الجُمْلَةُ الاِسْمِيَّةُ⁩ ) and move from one to the other;
2. grant the verb with the subject when he precedes it and when he follows it;
3. to give verbs, adjectives and pronouns with plural things (singular feminine);
4. build sentences with an indefinite subject ( ⁧فِي المَكْتَبِ رَجُلٌ⁩ , ⁧عِنْدِي سُؤَالٌ⁩ );
5. recognize the nominal titles and the verbal text of the articles, and the order with the pronomial complement ( ⁧زَارَنِي⁩
6. accord the verb with the coordinated subjects and collective names.
Two-week plan.

2. Two types of phrase
⁧رَفَعَتِ الحُكُومَةُ الأُجُورَ.⁩ ⁧الحُكُومَةُ رَفَعَتِ الأُجُورَ.⁩ The government has increased wages.
— ⁧الطَّقْسُ جَمِيلٌ.⁩ The weather is good.

The verbal sentence begins with the verb: verb + subject ( ⁧فَاعِل⁩ ) + complements. It is the normal order of narrative and chronicle. The nominal sentence begins with a name, the term "theme" ( ⁧مُبْتَدَأ⁩ ), followed by what is said about it, the "predicate" ( ⁧خَبَر⁩ ). The predicate may be an adjective, a name, a preposition with its complement, or a verbal sentence: ⁧الحُكُومَةُ رَفَعَتِ الأُجُورَ⁩ = theme ⁧الحُكُومَةُ⁩ + predicate ⁧رَفَعَتِ الأُجُورَ.⁩ What's the difference? The content is the same; It changes the focus. The nominal sentence highlights the subject (as far as the government is concerned, increased wages) or contrasts it with another. In the spoken language and dialects the SVO order is much more frequent than in the fuṣḥā written.
3. The agreement in the verbal sentence (verb first)
Rule: the verb before the subject remains to the singular, but it accords in the genre.

Two cases to be recognized. 1. If there are other words between the verb and the female subject, the verb may remain to the male: ⁧حَضَرَ الاِجْتِمَاعَ ثَلَاثُ مُوَظَّفَاتٍ⁩ Three staff members attended the meeting (but ⁧حَضَرَتْ⁩ is always correct). 2. With a plural over people, in the literary language the verb sometimes goes to female: ⁧قَالَتِ الأَعْرَابُ⁩ . In the newspapers you will almost always find the male: ⁧قَالَ الخُبَرَاءُ.⁩ The pronoun subject is inside the verb and does not repeat: ⁧وَصَلُوا⁩ They're here. When the subject has already been appointed, the verb takes the desinence of person: ⁧وَصَلَ الوُزَرَاءُ وَعَقَدُوا اجْتِمَاعًا⁩ The Ministers arrived and held a meeting.
4. The agreement in the nominal sentence (verb after)
Rule: the verb after the subject agrees in everything: gender and number.
dual ⁧الوَزِيرَتَانِ وَصَلَتَا.⁩ · ⁧الوَزِيرَانِ وَصَلَا.⁩ The two ministers/the two minions have arrived.
The same applies to the preaching adjectives: ⁧الطُّلَّابُ مُتْعَبُونَ⁩ , ⁧الطَّالِبَاتُ مُتْعَبَاتٌ.⁩
5. The pluralities of things and animals
Rule: a non-human plural ( ⁧جَمْعُ غَيْرِ العَاقِلِ⁩ ) is a singular female, in any position: verb, adjective, pronoun, demonstrative.

7. The Indeterminate Subject: The Predicate Before
A nominal sentence does not normally start with an indefinite name. If the subject is indeterminate, the predicate (a preposition with its complement, a place adverb) goes ahead:

rows: There's a man in the office waiting for you.
There's a car in front of the house.

blocks.text: ⁧هُنَاكَ حَلٌّ آخَرُ.⁩ There is another solution.

Determined or indefinite? With the determined subject the normal order is theme + predicate: ⁧الرَّجُلُ فِي المَكْتَبِ⁩ The man is in the office. With the undetermined entity: ⁧فِي المَكْتَبِ رَجُلٌ⁩ There's a man in the office. In Italian, the difference often corresponds to "è" / "c'è" is ".

Nominal title, verbal text It is the press convention:

⁧تَظَاهَرَ آلَافُ الطُّلَّابِ أَمْسِ فِي وَسَطِ العَاصِمَةِآلَافُ الطُّلَّابِ يَتَظَاهَرُونَ فِي العَاصِمَةِ⁩ …

blocks.text: In the title, the verb is often imperfect even for a past fact: it is a journalistic present, like the Italian "The government increases wages" . The pronoun complement. When the object is a pronoun, it attaches itself to the verb and the subject comes after: ⁧زَارَنِي صَدِيقٌ⁩ A friend visited me, ⁧أَخْبَرَنَا المَسْؤُولُ⁩ The person in charge informed us. In Italian, it is often better to put the subject back before: "A friend came to visit me." The theme with the pronoun of recovery. To highlight an element you take it to the beginning and resume it with a pronoun: ⁧المُدِيرُ، تَحَدَّثْتُ مَعَهُ أَمْسِ⁩ The director, I spoke to him yesterday. ⁧هٰذَا الكِتَابُ قَرَأْتُهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ⁩ I've read this book twice. It is frequent in the most lively of the spoken and journalistic texts.
9. Coordinated entities and collective names

Coordinated subjects. If the verb precedes, it agrees with the first subject: ⁧وَصَلَ الوَزِيرُ وَالوَفْدُ⁩ ; ⁧حَضَرَتْ مَرْيَمُ وَزَوْجُهَا⁩ . If it follows, go to the dual or plural: ⁧الوَزِيرُ وَالوَفْدُ وَصَلَا⁩ ; ⁧مَرْيَمُ وَزَوْجُهَا حَضَرَا.⁩ Collective names. They agree according to their grammatical form:
10. Pronunciation

The desinences they decide. In a nominal phrase read aloud, the endings show who the subject is: ⁧الحُكُومَةُ رَفَعَتِ الأُجُورَ⁩ The subject, a on the object. Read section tables 3–5 with all the endings, then paused (without the final vowel). The intonation of the nominal phrase. In a sentence with the theme in relief ( ⁧المُدِيرُ، تَحَدَّثْتُ مَعَهُ⁩ ) there is a short pause after the theme: signal the comma with the voice.
